Reading excluding character strings chosen. Inside a charstring literal "?" is an ordinary character, so the only way to violate the rule is element-list notation for a charstring value; the rejection may also be caused by that notation itself.
Titan reports too few elements for array template {1, *}; the standard explicitly allows AnyElementsOrNone inside arrays (see example MyStrings in B.1.3.2.0).
Longest-match is not directly observable through a boolean match result; the test checks cases where * must absorb repeated elements equal to the following symbol.
Titan does not support map types; warning ignored.
As for B.1.3.1.0-002a: "*" in a charstring literal is a plain character, so element-list notation of a charstring is used to place * inside a character string value.
Reading 'combined pattern' chosen: templates that only match if permutation and AnyElementsOrNone are considered together (e.g. {permutation(1,*),2} against {3,1,2}).
Titan rejects '* length(1)' as element of a record of integer; the standard explicitly allows it (NOTE 2 and B.1.4.1).
Titan rejects 'omit length(2)'; the standard explicitly allows it.
Titan rejects 'omit length(2)'; the standard explicitly allows it.
Titan rejects '* length(2)' as record of element; the standard's own example uses {1, * length(2), 3}.
Uses a length restriction on a value range (not in the allowed list). Titan does not implement this check.
Per BNF (BaseTemplateBody ::= SimpleSpec [ExtraMatchingAttributes]) the length attribute applies to the whole concatenation "ab" & ?, which is prohibited.
Titan does not support template concatenation with matching symbols (clause 15.11); warning ignored.
